whyChoose.title: Why This Matters Under California Law

items.title: Time Limits Apply
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim, though claims against a government agency can require notice in as little as six months. Acting sooner helps preserve evidence and options.

items.title: Shared Fault Doesn't Bar You
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover damages — just reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California does not limit the amount of non-economic damages, such as compensation for pain and suffering, that a jury may award.

items.title: No Upfront Cost to You
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no fee unless we recover money on your behalf. This lets injured people pursue a claim without paying out of pocket.

items.question: How much time do I have to file a claim in Biggs?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity was involved, the notice window can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking your situation promptly.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so being partially responsible doesn't stop you from recovering compensation. Your total award would simply be reduced by the percentage of fault assigned to you.
